meta.description: Fabio "naif" Pietrosanti (石风翱): hacker since 1995, then entrepreneur and innovator. Today biohacking, digital rights and national security. Thirty years of talks, press, research and open-source work, with sources and local copies.

story.title: The hacker scene and the first security jobs
body: Fabio started in information security in 1995 inside the Italian hacker community, where he is still known as naif. By the late 1990s he was writing in BFi (the s0ftpj e-zine) and contributing to Italian Linux documentation such as Linux Domande e Risposte.

In 2000–2001 he co-founded Sikurezza.org, one of the reference Italian security communities and mailing lists, and was a founding member of the Italian Black Hats, launched at SMAU 2001. In 2002 La Stampa followed him and other Black Hats around Milan testing the security of wireless networks.

Meanwhile the hobby became a profession: CTO of Live Network Security, freelance ICT-security writer for Mondadori's WeekIT and for ICT Security, network security manager at I.NET — where he designed a Security Operation Center — and from 2004 senior information-security consultant reporting to the security CTO of Telecom Italia. Talks from those years cover wireless insecurity (Webbit, SMAU, CNR), anonymous communication (hack.lu 2006) and PGP (e-privacy 2005).

story.title: Voice encryption and the honesty of the crypto market
body: In 2005 he co-founded KHAMSA, later PrivateWave Italia, building mobile voice and messaging encryption (PrivateGSM) for governments and enterprises, and worked with Philip Zimmermann on a ZRTP-based encrypted transport for circuit-switched networks. PrivateWave released ZORG, an open-source C++ and Java ZRTP implementation, in 2011 — the year ZRTP became RFC 6189.

Two international patents came out of that work, filed by KHAMSA Italia with Federico Moro and Lorenzo Boccaccia: WO2008015721 / EP2057808, secure management of multiple identities in centralised messaging services, and WO2008015723 / EP2057777, a method to record a non-repudiable digital communication and identify its participants (see Patents).

On his blog infosecurity.ch he wrote about mobile and voice security and exposed how parts of the market worked: in 2010 he showed that a supposedly independent review of voice-encryption products was traceable to one of the vendors (picked up by The Register), and he wrote against snake-oil claims and marketing “hacking contests”. With others he released OSXCrypt (2008), an attempt to bring TrueCrypt-compatible disk encryption to macOS.

story.title: Whistleblowing and anonymity infrastructure
body: In 2010 he started GlobaLeaks, free software for secure and anonymous whistleblowing, and in December 2010 built the Hermes Center for Transparency and Digital Human Rights around it; Hermes has been a member of European Digital Rights (EDRi) since 2018. Hermes also rewrote and maintained Tor2web, the gateway that lets ordinary browsers reach Tor onion services.

GlobaLeaks became the base of whistleblowing platforms run by newsrooms, NGOs and public bodies — from Publeaks in the Netherlands and IRPILeaks to anti-corruption channels with Transparency International Italy and, later, the Italian anti-corruption authority. Since 2016 Whistleblowing Solutions, a non-profit social enterprise, turns that technology into a sustainable service.

He has been a regular in the Tor community since 2011: running exit relays and Tor2web nodes, taking part in the international Tor developers' meetings, and opening tickets that changed Tor itself — OutboundBindAddressExit, shipped in Tor 0.3.0, comes from his 2016 proposal for low-liability exit relays.

story.title: Policy, surveillance and democracy
body: The same method moved into policy. In 2017 he was one of the proponents of the Italian bill on state trojans (captatori informatici) presented by Stefano Quintarelli, and he took the topic to e-privacy, Freedom Not Fear in Brussels and the CCC. He ran the 2017 campaign that pushed VideoLAN to serve VLC over HTTPS, mapped the risks of Kaspersky software in the Italian public sector (Euronews 2018, again in 2022) and used FOIA requests to monitor surveillance.

On electronic voting he wrote the Guida Hermes al voto digitale, analysed the 2017 Lombardy e-voting referendum, animated the CRVD committee, studied how Italians abroad could vote at polling stations (the AIRE study) and, with OpenRousseau, showed the weaknesses of the Five Star Movement's Rousseau platform — including by voting twice on it.
In 2022 Monitora PA, a civic-hacking project run with Hermes and volunteers, pushed thousands of Italian public administrations to remove Google Analytics.

story.title: Parcels, logistics and algorithmic finance
body: For thirteen years he worked in the family's GLS express-courier branch in Latina, bringing automation, measurement systems, cost control and ecological last-mile delivery into a business that moves parcels for a living. That work produced Haulersense (computer vision and revenue recovery for couriers), LESS.green and OpenPUDO — open-source software for pick-up and drop-off networks — and PLogistics, an e-commerce fulfilment operation. In 2022 he taught the logistics of pick-up points at LIUC University.
Since 2019 he has led SignalSwarm in Dubai: a fully automated, market-neutral trading platform and the asset-management service built on it.

story.title: Biohacking and open human data
body: Since 2023 he has been building biohack.it with the Hacking Biology Foundation: AGPL-licensed, non-profit infrastructure where self-experimenters document protocols and standard-coded biomarkers, so that individual experiments become comparable human data. He has talked about it on Rai 1 (Codice), Rai Radio 1 (Codice Beta) and at the TimePie biohacker forum in Shanghai.

GlobaLeaks: Free and open-source software for secure, anonymous whistleblowing, started in 2010 and used worldwide by newsrooms, NGOs, companies and public administrations.
Tor2web: Gateway that lets ordinary browsers reach Tor onion services. Originally created by Aaron Swartz and Virgil Griffith, rewritten and maintained by the Hermes Center from 2011.
Hermes Center for Transparency and Digit: Non-profit association founded in December 2010 to develop transparency and anonymity technologies and to do digital-rights advocacy. EDRi member since 2018.
Whistleblowing Solutions / Whistleblowin: Non-profit social enterprise (2016) offering GlobaLeaks as a service; WhistleblowingPA made a free whistleblowing channel available to Italian public administrations.
PrivateGSM / PrivateWave (cifratura voce: Mobile voice and messaging encryption for governments and enterprises, built by PrivateWave Italia (2005–2014), with ZRTP-based designs developed with Philip Zimmermann.
ZORG — implementazione open source di ZR: Open-source C++ and Java implementation of ZRTP released by PrivateWave in January 2011.
OSXCrypt: 2008 open-source release bringing TrueCrypt-compatible disk encryption to macOS, with Orlando Bassotto and Matteo Flora.
Tor exit node e honeypot sugli hidden se: Operating Tor exit and Tor2web nodes from 2011 and studying abuse and noisy traffic on them.
Trojans and Rule of Law — proposta di le: Italian bill on state hacking tools presented by Stefano Quintarelli in 2017; Fabio was one of its proponents, together with lawyers and technologists. Presented in Italy, at the CCC and at Freedom Not Fear in Brussels.
Guida Hermes al voto digitale: Hermes Center guide to the risks of digital voting (2017).
CRVD voto elettronico: Committee on the requirements of voting in a democracy: analyses and articles on e-voting (2018–2020). Site preserved in 2026.
Progetto AIRE (voto degli italiani all'e: 2019 geolocation study of Italians registered abroad: 80 overseas polling stations would cover more than 86% of voters — an alternative to online voting.
OpenRousseau: Open-source counter-platform (2020) exposing the weaknesses of the Five Star Movement's Rousseau voting system.
Voto elettronico referendum Lombardia 20: Analysis and FOIA requests on the voting machines used in the 2017 Lombardy autonomy referendum.
Monitora PA (rimozione Google Analytics: Civic-hacking project (2022) that measured Italian public websites and pushed thousands of administrations to remove Google Analytics.
Kaspersky: matrice dei rischi e uso nell: Risk matrix of using Kaspersky software in the Italian public sector, if the vendor were forced to cooperate with the Russian government (2018, updated 2022).
mxmap.it / Osservatorio Nazionale Sovran: Map of which providers handle the email of Italian public administrations, and an observatory on digital sovereignty (2026).
Italian Hacker Camp / Italian Hacker Emb: The Italian hacker gatherings: End Summer Camp in Venice, the Italian Hacker Camp in Padova and the Italian Hacker Embassy village at the Dutch and German camps (since CCCamp 2007).
Sikurezza.org: Italian security community and mailing lists, co-founded around 2000; presented at Webbit and Security Summit.
Italian Black Hats: Association of Italian security researchers launched at SMAU 2001; founding member.
biohack.it / Hacking Biology Foundation: Open infrastructure for structured human self-experimentation: protocols, standard-coded biomarkers and shared outcomes (AGPL-3.0, non-profit, since 2023).
LESS.green — last mile sostenibile: Non-profit tech start-up for low-emission last-mile delivery in e-commerce (2020–2023), publishing its software on GitHub.
Haulersense: AI and computer-vision tools for couriers: weight and volume revenue recovery, parcel-machine telemetry and shipping analytics (2019–2023).
Aeroporto di Latina: Civic campaign for Latina airport as the third airport of Lazio (2026).
Sendmail.cf backdoor, chrooted, firewall: Early security code and research published 2000–2002.
OSSCI / OSPCI — Osservatorio Sicurezza d: Proposal (2019) for an observatory actively measuring the security of Italy's national cyber perimeter, reviewed by dozens of engineers and lawyers and supported by more than 250 people — years before the national cybersecurity agency existed. It never started.
COVID-19: mappatura dei focolai con i da: Proposal during the pandemic to map outbreaks from mobile-network cell data. It never started.
COVID-19: vulnerabilità dell'app COVID d: Security analysis of the Lazio region's COVID app, with Giovanni Rocca (2020).
OpenPUDO — primo software open source pe: Open-source software for pick-up and drop-off point networks, released by LESS in 2021.
ifuriosi.it — archivio delle evidenze e: Archive of evidence (2020) linking the ifuriosi.it site and its Philip Morris advertising to infrastructure shared with Casaleggio Associati.
LIUC 2022 — intervento sui punti di riti: Lecture on pick-up points at LIUC University's conference with SOS LOGistica (29 September 2022).
SecurStar/PhoneCrypt — debunking di una: 2010 evidence that a supposedly independent review of voice-encryption products was run by one of the vendors; covered by The Register.
Snake oil nella cifratura voce: marketin: 2009–2010 writing against unverifiable security claims and marketing contests in voice encryption.
Tor exit node a bassa responsabilità (20: From running an exit node to changing Tor: the proposal for exit-only outbound addresses became OutboundBindAddressExit in Tor 0.3.0.
Analisi della sicurezza e della scelta d: 2010 analysis of elliptic-curve choices in proprietary crypto products.
VLC over HTTPS — campagna per il downloa: 2017 campaign after the CIA leaks: tickets, a census of 35 HTTPS mirrors and a proof of concept pushed VideoLAN towards HTTPS downloads.

communities: Co-founder and president since 2010. EDRi member since 2018.

Since 1995: s0ftpj/BFi, Sikurezza.org, Italian Black Hats, Hackmeeting, End Summer Camp, the Italian Hacker Camp and the Italian Hacker Embassy at CCCamp, HAR, OHM, SHA and the Chaos Communication Congress.

A regular of the Tor community: Tor exit-relay and Tor2web node operator, participant in the international Tor developers' meetings, contributor of tickets and proposals — two of them shipped in Tor 0.2.6 and 0.3.0.
Speaker, moderator and Big Brother Awards presenter at e-privacy since 2005.
Member 2014–2021, bridge with Hermes on whistleblowing.
Member: working group on online voting (2019), dialogues on facial recognition (2020) and privacy coins (2023).

truth_intro: Most of this work has one shape: someone claims something — a vendor, a ministry, a platform, a political movement — and the claim is taken on trust because nobody can check it. The answer is always the same: build the tool that makes it checkable, publish the evidence, and let other people verify it themselves.

That is why the software is free and open source, why the evidence sits in public repositories, why the requests to public bodies are filed under freedom-of-information law and published together with their answers, and why every claim on this page links to its source. When the finding was uncomfortable, it was published anyway: in 2020 he showed that the Rousseau platform could not guarantee the integrity of a vote — by voting twice on it. That was activism against the Five Star Movement, against the technological control that a private company, Casaleggio Associati, exercised over an Italian political party. He was expelled for it, and published the expulsion documents.

Concretely: free software that lets newsrooms receive documents from anonymous sources, training for the journalists who use it, transparency requests that force public data into the open, and a handful of investigations run first-hand.
truth_strands_note: Every item below is in the archive, with a link to the source and, where possible, a local copy.

identity.role_note: Hacker first — the rest came out of it.

focus_now_title: Hacker since 1995 — that one never ends. Open-source hacktivism since 1997, cybersecurity since 2001, and the three that matter most right now.

focus_now.text: From the Italian hacker scene — the BFi e-zine, Italian Linux documentation, Sikurezza.org, Hackmeeting, End Summer Camp — to a simple rule kept ever since: what he builds ships as free software. ZORG, OSXCrypt, Tor2web, GlobaLeaks, OpenPUDO, biohack.it.

The profession: security operations and threat analysis at I.NET, counter-intelligence and security research at Telecom Italia, published advisories, the Italian Black Hats, then ten years of mobile voice encryption at PrivateWave — two international patents — and, ever since, security work in the open: the VLC HTTPS campaign, TLS and Tor tickets.

Hermes Center and GlobaLeaks: whistleblowing and anonymity technology used by newsrooms, NGOs and public bodies, plus the advocacy around it — surveillance, state trojans, biometrics, public-sector privacy.

Measuring the digital dependencies of a country instead of debating them: the Kaspersky risk matrix, the OSSCI proposal for an observatory on the national cyber perimeter, and mxmap.it on who really runs the infrastructure of Italian public administration.
biohack.it and the Hacking Biology Foundation: open infrastructure that turns individual self-experimentation into comparable human data — protocols, standard-coded biomarkers, results in the open.

evidence_title: Same four steps every time: a claim, a check anyone can repeat, the evidence published, an outcome.

steps: An “independent” review scored 12 of 15 voice-encryption products as broken.
Domains, servers and writing style traced the site back to one of the vendors.
Five posts with the technical evidence on infosecurity.ch.
Picked up by The Register and CSO; the “independent researcher” disappeared.

evidence.case: Kaspersky in the Italian public sector
steps: Antivirus from a Russian vendor was installed across ministries and police forces.
A public risk matrix of what that vendor could do if coerced by its government.
Repository and interviews, in 2018 and again in 2022.
Euronews, then national coverage during the war; the issue reached government decisions.
A private company ran the voting platform of an Italian political party.
Registered twice and voted twice, documenting every step.
The method, the documents and the expulsion papers, published in full.
Covered by Wired; the platform's integrity claims could no longer be repeated.
Thousands of public websites sent citizens' data to Google by default.
Automated scans of public administrations, with the legal reasoning attached.
Notices to the administrations and to the data-protection authority, all public.
Thousands of public sites removed Google Analytics; the authority ruled on it.
